item.content:encoded: So many 001's lately. Looks like everybody wants a spot on the page now. Unfortunately, the SCP itself feels much too mundane for 001 - there are probably a hundred SCPs that can keep people alive forever with no side effects and less ethical problems, so this one is no different from many others. There's been a literal fountain of youth+health for almost ten years now. It also notably does not seem to address anything related to aging or general health. Nor does it hit on the "why are there so many SPCs here anyway" angle which, while not strictly necessary, is used by the great 001's to show why they should be 001 instead of 7592. Don't mean to be a Negative Nedry, and I think this would have been a good general skip, but good isn't good enough for 001.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While I respect your personal interpretation of what an 001 proposal should be, I would like to simply recognize that it is just an interpretation, and what I would personally call it a limiting one.

In-universe, this is supposed to be an SCP slot. Subject to the same format controls the Foundation imposes on all other entries, barring some very good reason to relax their rules.

Furthermore, I'd like to bring up one of the central tenants of SCP articles - "There Is No Canon". Therefore, while you can dislike this because it does not jive with what you want the 001 slot to be, this blanket statement implies that this is a hard and fast rule about 001s, which is simply not the case. There is no canon. Therefore there is no "what an 001 needs to be".

Again, I respect your reasoning for not liking this, but the way you've phrased this comment implies that this article breaks universal 001 rules, which do not exist.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love this story and every element of it.
Particularly fond of this version of the Ethics Committee, both morally and procedurally plausible. Not an pro forma conscious-soother, disregarded joke, or any of the other half-satisfying characterizations I've seen before.

But this isn't a good 001. In-universe, this is supposed to be an SCP slot. Subject to the same format controls the Foundation imposes on all other entries, barring some very good reason to relax their rules. There is no justification given for these chat sessions to even be recorded, much less be included in the (nominally) strictly structured scientific database.

It's become expected for a 001 to play with the format, but this went a step too far off the path for the space it aspires to.

So, yeah. Great tale I'd upvote many times over, but downvote since it falls short of what a 001 should be… Not that I harbor any delusions of changing the course of opinion with +100 and counting.

item.title: ethics
item.content:encoded: I do so enjoy seeing people do interesting things with the Ethics Committee.

I'm a long-time lurker and had to make an account to comment on this because I enjoyed it so much!

+ Thoughts and feedback
- Sorry I am so verbose...

At the beginning, I saw several tropes, especially as an 001 proposal: it opens with a terminal clearance prompt, it's thaumiel, it's literally death, the Foundation's using it how you'd expect complete with non-apology addendum (reminiscent of 110-montauk). But the rest of the SCP… I am not sure if you intended to set up the reader's expectations like that to subvert them. The rest of the tale was brilliant.

My favorite aspect, overall, is how the AIC dialogue is used to reveal the narrative. I'm used to seeing terminal logs of this kind in SCPs to make them seem top-level uber-classified. I love that you made the AIC show - not just tell - the story, as it happens, that the AIC were active characters in the tale, not just a prop.

"Targeted prosopagnosia" is genius. I love that you incorporated science here rather than cheating Death through purely Arcane means. A small thing but it reflects the unique juxtaposition of science and the supernatural in the SCP universe.

I found several other details to be masterful. The music request was an excellent touch. It lent so much emotion to the scene once it clicked for me.

My main critique, is that the description of SCP-001 itself was confusing and handwavy when it comes to the connection between SCP-001 and death. It's unclear to me how it behaves and why. For instance:
- Why does it have complete lack of response to stimuli?
- How does the Foundation know the prosopagnosia succeeded, if SCP-001 lacks response to stimuli?
- How can SCP-001's own death be impending? He's old, but he's also conceptually merged with death so shouldn't he stay alive until he percieves himself as dead?
- The containment procedures mention "calibrations" but this was not explained (unless I missed it, or unless maybe "calibrations" refers to the specific people he has prosopagnosia to?)
- Why did it "wake up" and respond to the Administrator? This is a plot hole to me, as it's stated to be the first time it responds to anything, but I'm confused as to why?

Are "Erikeshan" and "The Eternal Circle" references to something? I do like that SCP-001 has a backstory but I'd suggest linking these or providing footnotes for the unfamiliar. Seeing proper nouns like that, I want to know more of the lore behind them.

Thanks for bearing with this verbose response - I hope it helps :)

item.title: Re: Oh hey, this again
item.content:encoded:
Even if you find it to be ridiculous, it's not unrealistic. There are plenty of extremely modern examples of leaders ignoring the advice of their ethics departments.1 Things might generally be better off if Overseers and the Ethics Commitee worked together on issues instead of stonewalling each other or trying to apply additional pressure, but people have interests that can be separate from the interests of institutions as a whole.

As I said, you can not enjoy it as a story, but it's not an absurd state of affairs.

Footnotes
1. I'd rather not make this about politics, but some simple googling will give you these.

item.title: Re: Oh hey, this again
item.content:encoded:
I think this is a pretty shallow way of looking at the situation. Why have an Ethics Committee at all? To assure people that their behavior is ethical, or to accuse others of unethical behavior. If it's staffed with lapdogs to the Overseers, those assurances don't have a whole lot of meaning. Any kind of ethics evaluation (or any other kind of compliance) has to have some measure of independence or else everyone knows it's baseless. This is a long-running problem in real governments and industries.

Loyalty means different things to different people. Is letting the Overseers do what they want without objection loyal to the Foundation as an institution, even if they're betraying core ideals? I wouldn't say so, personally. There's a similar argument from the Overseers if they believe the Ethics Committee is acting outside of its established purview, etc.

Add weird paramilitaries being tied to bureaucratic authority, interpersonal conflict between powerful people, and the presence of existentially threatening issues, and there's plenty that makes this kind of conflict realistic.

It's fine if it doesn't fit into your headcanon, but I don't think your argument against it as a narrative concept holds a lot of weight.

In an earlier draft, '(see classified death figures enclosed)' was '(an investigation into the rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is ongoing)'. If that would improve the article for you or anyone else, I'd be happy to change it.

The thing about the Administrator is that he's fine with necessary evil — his feelings that the Foundation would be objectively good faded pretty quickly once things got going — but he feels that what the O5 are doing with 001 isn't necessary at all. To add to that, it's having visible negative side-effects on the world that partially go against the mission of the Foundation. If putting the concept of death into a person and messing around with it were needed to, say, contain SCP-2317 or something, nobody would bat an eye.

But since it's purely for the benefit of the O5 Council — and they're clearly lying about using this to preserve other vital Foundation personnel — it's something the Administrator can't ignore, so he quietly sends a message to the Chairman.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
No-voting — this was a hard one for me. On one hand, I love the fundamental anomaly (the notion of physically personifying a concept, then having actions taken against that person impact the concept itself). There's a lot of bits here I also really liked — the idea of the Ethics Committee equivalent of the Red Hand, the casual mention of members of the O5 council being shot in the head and 'not dead' — etc.

On the other hand…

FEEDBACK
– hide block
  • The final interview between the Administrator and the 001 fell rather flat for me; it gave me a strong vibe of 'trying to feel profound'.
  • On one hand, I kind of like the hypocrisy of the O5 council (I liked how the note mentioned expanding 001's effect to others, then we discover that they've selected no one to expand it to). On the other hand, I kind of don't — this reduces the O5 council to the Injustice League. I think a more compelling story here would have been something involving a few (or even just one) O5s abusing the anomaly.
  • The AI stuff was kind of cute, but also didn't work for me. I couldn't figure out what their dialogue really added, on the whole. I feel like the story could have been communicated much more cleanly and effectively as an epistolary piece (via emails, perhaps).
  • Finally, I feel very much like this fits as more of a story/tale than an 001. I'm sure you're going to get a lot of that (and I'm sure you were expecting it); in a sense, this is in the same boat as When Day Breaks — but while I feel When Day Breaks works as an 001, I feel as if this doesn't. It's hard for me to pin down precisely why — I think certain elements of the piece just didn't hook me. It might just be that my standards for 001s are much higher than my standards for tales.

Regardless, at the very least, I enjoyed the writing in this piece and several of the ideas you presented. It seems like I might be (mostly) alone on feeling like this doesn't work as an 001 (which is quite fine; different tastes and aesthetics, after all). Good luck with it!
